hook.line: Every call to the coast crackles. Tomás keeps saying *what?* in English, when he could just say that the line is bad.
hook.es: No te oigo bien, se oye muy mal.
hook.en: I can't hear you well, the line's really bad.

examples.es: No te oigo bien, se oye muy mal.
examples.en: I can't hear you well, the line's really bad.

examples.es: Desde aquí no se ve nada.
examples.en: You can't see anything from here.

examples.es: No te escucho bien, ¿me oyes tú?
examples.en: I can't hear you well, can you hear me?
You can hear really well here.
Sorry, I can't see him well.

rule:
To say how well you see or hear, use the verb with *bien*, *mal* or *nada*:
*No te oigo bien.* *Lo veo mal.* *No se ve nada.*

On the phone in Latin America, *escuchar* is as common as *oír*: *No te escucho bien*.

To talk about the place or the line rather than you, add *se*: *Se oye mal*, *Aquí se ve bien*. English says *you can hear* or *it sounds bad*.

To ask someone to speak up, use *voz*: *en voz alta*, *en voz más alta* (louder), *en voz baja* (quietly). Never *más alto* for volume.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *se* in *se oye mal* the impersonal *se*: nobody in particular is doing the hearing.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *oigo* or *oyes*: No te ___ bien. (I can't hear you) Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: I can't hear you: the verb is *oigo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: You can hardly hear anything here.
yourTurn.why: *No se oye nada* means you can't hear a thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The line's really bad. (it sounds really bad)
Ask a man you call *usted* to speak louder.
Say: You can't see anything from here.
yourTurn.answer: Desde aquí no se ve nada.
yourTurn.why: *No se ve nada* is the usual way to say you can't see a thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: I can't hear you well.
yourTurn.why: *Escuchar* and *oír* are both fine on the phone.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about seeing: *No te oigo bien.*

pitfalls.why: Almost. For how well you hear, use *bien*, not *bueno*.
The *no* goes first: *No te oigo bien*.

personal: Think of the last bad phone call you had. Write what you'd say to the other person, using *no te oigo bien* or *se oye mal*.
